study.title: SqueezeSlimU-Net: An Adaptive and Efficient Segmentation Architecture for Real-Time UAV Weed Detection
study.short_title: SSU-Net slimmable Squeeze U-Net: IoU 58.28%, 2.5M params, 4.25-9.09 FPS in-flight
study.venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing

segmentation.domain: real-time UAV weed detection via dynamically slimmable network width (Squeeze U-Net + SqueezeNet fire modules + slimmable neural networks), validated on an onboard edge platform (Jetson Nano) with Monsoon power measurement
models_tested: AlexNet (0.7 GFLOPS) as input-complexity adaptation classifier
segmentation.best_model: SSU-Net at 100% width: IoU 58.28%, accuracy 90.47%, recall 62.89% on AgriAdapt (512x512), with only 2.5M parameters; on par with DeepLabV3 (IoU 58.35%, 11.0 M) and FCN (IoU 62.62%, 35.3 M). SU-Net (non-squeezed) scores higher IoU 63.58% on the Tobacco dataset but is up to 6.8x slower/per-inference energy.

dataset.name: AgriAdapt weed detection dataset, first partition (497 UAV images of salad crops, Rome, Italy, Autumn 2023) - primary; validated also on Tobacco Aerial Dataset campaign 2 (936 UAV images, Mavic Mini, Mardan, Pakistan, April 2021)
dataset.note: Custom built 6 kg hexacopter with onboard NVIDIA Jetson Nano and Arducam 16 MP Sony IMX519 camera on a 2-axis brushless gimbal (AgriAdapt). 80/20 train/test split; images resampled to 512x512 (optimum); background and crop merged into a single class (binary weed detection); weighted CE loss 0.1/0.9 background/weed + L2 0.01; max 300 epochs, Adam lr 1e-4 decay 0.99, batch 8.

segmentation.backbone: SSU-Net: U-Net skeleton, SqueezeNet fire modules (squeeze/expand with SlimmableConv2d + SwitchableBatchNorm2d), slimmable transposed convolutions; widths 100/75/50/25%

mIoU.quote: At 100% width, the SSU-Net achieved an IoU of 58.28%, surpassing the SU-Net's 57.13%
mIoU.ambiguity: Binary weed-vs-background IoU on AgriAdapt (512x512), SSU-Net 100% width; IoU 53% at 25% width and 51.67% to 59.67% across widths on Tobacco.

mPA.ambiguity: Accuracy reported is overall/semantic-segmentation accuracy (OA), not class-mean.

F1.quote: The F1-score, balancing precision and recall, also highlights the SSU-Net's dominance, which scores better at the top three widths
F1.ambiguity: F1-score is reported for SSU-Net vs SU-Net per width in Table III, but numeric values are not recoverable from the extracted text.

PA.quote: At 100% width, it achieved an accuracy of 90.47%, compared to the SU-Net's 89.41%
PA.ambiguity: Overall pixel accuracy (OA) of SSU-Net 100% width on AgriAdapt; drops to ~88% at narrower widths. Comparable state-of-the-art models reach 90-91% accuracy.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Binary weed-vs-background F1 reported only via overall F1-score (Table III), not separate per-class weed/crop F1.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Crop merged into background; no per-crop F1 reported.

edge.device: NVIDIA Jetson Nano 4 GB board (Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS, Python 3.8.10, PyTorch 1.12.0), commonly mounted onboard UAVs; power measured with a Monsoon power monitor tool
edge.framework: PyTorch (trained on NVIDIA RTX 3090 24 GB, batch 8, Adam lr 1e-4 exp-decay 0.99, max 300 epochs early-stopped); TorchScript deployment on Jetson Nano; no quantization NCHW

fps.quote: FPS, ranging from 4.25 for the 100% width network to 9.09 for the 25% width
fps.ambiguity: Average FPS on Jetson Nano at 512x512 across slimmable widths (100%: 4.25, 25%: 9.09); meets 4.5 FPS real-time benchmark threshold; SU-Net stays below 4 FPS on the same hardware.

latency_ms.quote: TU-Net. The exhibited differences in inference time make an essential distinction between a solution that enables real-time inference and a solution that does not allow such operation
latency_ms.ambiguity: Derived as 1000/4.25 FPS for the 100%-width model on Jetson Nano; ~110 ms at 25% width. Raw per-instance times are given in Fig. 5(b) only (up to 6.8x faster than SU-Net) - value estimated from reported FPS.

power_w.quote: In the case of the Tobacco dataset, the results show that as the energy consumption decreases threefold (from 0.1 to 0.03 mAh), the average IoU declines by just 3%
power_w.ambiguity: Power in watts not reported; per-inference energy measured with Monsoon power monitor: ~0.1 mAh (100% width) to 0.03 mAh (25% width) on Tobacco; up to 65% energy saving with ~2% accuracy drop via input-based adaptation.

params_M.quote: With 2.5 M parameters, SSU-Net achieves an IoU of 58.28%, closely matching larger models, such as Deeplab V3 (58.35%, 11.0 M)
params_M.ambiguity: Parameter count at 100% width; decreases at 75/50/25% widths via slimming. Compare FCN 35.3 M, SegNet 29.44 M, U-Net 0.5 M.

gflops.quote: With its eight layers (five convolutional and three fully connected), and only 0.7 GFLOPS, AlexNet is a powerful yet reasonably small architecture
gflops.ambiguity: SSU-Net GFLOPS not explicitly stated in extracted text; 0.7 GFLOPS figure is for the AlexNet input-complexity adaptation classifier.
